source_refs.note: Book p. 112-113: 6.9.2 definition of n H.Ms. and the method (n A.Ms. between 1/a and 1/b, then reciprocals), Example 25. Teaching notes, d formula, key points and common mistakes are ours.

items.title: 6.9.2 n Harmonic Means between two Numbers (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Pichle sabaq mein hum ne do numbers ke beech sirf ek harmonic mean daala tha. Ab agar beech mein ek se zyada numbers daalne hon, maslan teen ya paanch, to kya karein? Tareeqa wahi purana hai: ulta karo, A.P. mein kaam karo, wapas ulta karo. Bas yahan A.P. mein kai arithmetic means daalne hain, jo aap 6.3 (Arithmetic Means) mein seekh chuke hain.

Kitab ki definition: \(H_{1}, H_{2}, H_{3}, \dots, H_{n}\) ko \(a\) aur \(b\) ke darmiyan \(n\) harmonic means (H.Ms.) kehte hain agar \(a, H_{1}, H_{2}, H_{3}, \dots, H_{n}, b\) H.P. mein hon. Agar humein \(a\) aur \(b\) ke darmiyan \(n\) H.Ms. daalne hon, to pehle \(\frac{1}{a}\) aur \(\frac{1}{b}\) ke darmiyan \(n\) A.Ms. \(A_{1}, A_{2}, \dots, A_{n}\) nikaalte hain, phir un ke reciprocals lete hain. Yani \(\frac{1}{A_{1}}, \frac{1}{A_{2}}, \dots, \frac{1}{A_{n}}\) hi \(a\) aur \(b\) ke darmiyan required \(n\) H.Ms. hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
"Insert karna" (beech mein daalna) ka matlab hai khaali jagah bharna. Jab \(n\) means daal dein to list \(a, H_{1}, \dots, H_{n}, b\) mein kul \(n + 2\) terms ho jati hain: \(a\) pehli term aur \(b\) aakhri yani \((n+2)^{\text{th}}\) term. Isi ginti mein students sab se zyada ghalti karte hain.
Tareeqa qadam ba qadam:
1. Dono kinare ulte karo: \(\frac{1}{a}\) aur \(\frac{1}{b}\).
2. A.P. \(\frac{1}{a}, A_{1}, \dots, A_{n}, \frac{1}{b}\) mein \(a_{n+2} = a_{1} + (n+1)d\) laga kar \(d\) nikaalo.
3. \(A_{1} = \frac{1}{a} + d\), \(A_{2} = \frac{1}{a} + 2d\), isi tarah aage.
4. Har \(A\) ko wapas ulta karo: \(H_{1} = \frac{1}{A_{1}}\), \(H_{2} = \frac{1}{A_{2}}\), ...

blocks.text_alt: d equals (1 over b minus 1 over a) over (n plus 1)

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Upar wala formula hamari taraf se hai: \(\frac{1}{b} = \frac{1}{a} + (n+1)d\) se seedha nikalta hai, aur reciprocals wali A.P. ka common difference foran de deta hai. \(n + 1\) par ghor karein: jaise ek rassi par \(3\) gaanthein lagayein to rassi \(4\) hisson mein bat jati hai, waise hi \(n\) numbers daalne se \(n + 1\) barabar faasle bante hain.
Ab kitab ki misaal mein yeh tareeqa chala kar dekhte hain.

blocks.title: Example 25
blocks.problem: Find three harmonic means between \(\frac{1}{5}\) and \(\frac{1}{17}\).
steps:
Given: kinaron ke numbers \(\frac{1}{5}\) aur \(\frac{1}{17}\); beech mein \(n = 3\) harmonic means daalne hain.
To find: \(H_{1}, H_{2}, H_{3}\) taa ke \(\frac{1}{5}, H_{1}, H_{2}, H_{3}, \frac{1}{17}\) H.P. mein hon.
Method: sab se pehle hum kinaron ko ulta karenge (\(5\) aur \(17\)), un ke beech teen A.Ms. daalenge, aur aakhir mein un ko ulta kar denge.

Step 1: Reciprocals ki A.P. banayein
Maan lein \(A_{1}, A_{2}, A_{3}\) number \(5\) aur \(17\) ke darmiyan teen A.Ms. hain, yani
\[5, A_{1}, A_{2}, A_{3}, 17 \text{ are in A.P.}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{1}{5}\) ka reciprocal \(5\) aur \(\frac{1}{17}\) ka \(17\) hai. H.Ms. inhi A.Ms. ke reciprocals honge.

Step 2: Aakhri term par \(a_{n} = a_{1} + (n-1)d\) lagayein
\[17 = 5 + (5-1)d\]
\(\because a_{5} = 17\) aur \(a_{1} = 5\).
Kyun: A.P. mein \(3\) means aur \(2\) kinare, yani kul \(5\) terms hain. Is liye \(17\) paanchvi term hai. Dhyan dein: yahan \(n = 5\) hai, \(3\) nahin.

Step 3: \(d\) nikaalein
\[4d = 12\]
\[d = 3\]
Kyun: dono taraf se \(5\) minus kiya (\(17 - 5 = 12\)) aur \(4\) se divide kiya. Exam tip wala formula bhi yahi deta hai: \(\frac{17 - 5}{3 + 1} = 3\).

Step 4: Teen A.Ms.
\[A_{1} = 5 + 3 = 8\]
\[A_{2} = 5 + 2(3) = 11\]
\[A_{3} = 5 + 3(3) = 14\]
Kyun: A.Ms. A.P. ki doosri, teesri aur chauthi terms hain; har dafa \(d = 3\) jama hota hai.

Step 5: Wapas ulta karein
\[H_{1} = \dfrac{1}{8},\ H_{2} = \dfrac{1}{11},\ H_{3} = \dfrac{1}{14}\]
Kyun: H.Ms. A.Ms. ke reciprocals hain. Agar yahan ruk kar \(8, 11, 14\) likh diya to woh A.Ms. hain, H.Ms. nahin.

Tasdeeq:
\(\frac{1}{5}, \frac{1}{8}, \frac{1}{11}, \frac{1}{14}, \frac{1}{17}\) ke reciprocals \(5, 8, 11, 14, 17\) hain jo har dafa \(3\) barhte hain. Yani A.P., is liye yeh paanchon H.P. mein hain. Jawab sahi.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin: \(\frac{1}{2}\) aur \(\frac{1}{8}\) ke darmiyan do H.Ms. daalein.
Ulta karein: \(2, A_{1}, A_{2}, 8\) A.P. mein; yahan \(4\) terms hain.
\(8 = 2 + 3d \Rightarrow d = 2\), to \(A_{1} = 4\), \(A_{2} = 6\).
Wapas ulta: H.Ms. \(\frac{1}{4}\) aur \(\frac{1}{6}\). Tasdeeq: \(2, 4, 6, 8\) A.P. hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar \(\frac{1}{5}\) aur \(\frac{1}{17}\) ke darmiyan sirf ek H.M. chahiye ho, to kya 6.9.1 wala formula \(H = \frac{2ab}{a+b}\) aur aaj wala tareeqa ek hi jawab denge? Koshish kijiye: formula se \(H = \frac{2 \cdot \frac{1}{85}}{\frac{22}{85}} = \frac{1}{11}\), aur tareeqe se \(5, A, 17\) mein \(A = 11\), to \(H = \frac{1}{11}\). Dono barabar! Is se pata chalta hai ke 6.9.1 asal mein isi tareeqe ka \(n = 1\) wala case hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(a\) aur \(b\) ke darmiyan \(n\) H.Ms.: \(a, H_{1}, \dots, H_{n}, b\) H.P. mein.
2. \(\frac{1}{a}\) aur \(\frac{1}{b}\) ke darmiyan \(n\) A.Ms. daalo, phir ulta karo.
3. A.P. mein \(n + 2\) terms hain, is liye \(\frac{1}{b} = \frac{1}{a} + (n+1)d\).
4. Tasdeeq: poori list ke reciprocals ka common difference hona chahiye.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(\frac{1}{5}\) aur \(\frac{1}{17}\) ke beech seedhe A.Ms. daal dena: yeh arithmetic means honge, harmonic nahin. Pehle kinare ulte karein.
2. Terms ki ghalat ginti: \(3\) means ke saath aakhri term paanchvi hai, is liye \((5-1)d\), \((3-1)d\) nahin.
3. A.Ms. \(8, 11, 14\) ko hi jawab likh dena: H.Ms. in ke reciprocals hain. Bachne ke liye jawab likhte waqt sawal ka lafz "harmonic" dobara parhein.
